dedupe_keys.name: northeast mexico household electricity and weather at one minute intervals

description: This dataset combines electricity measurements from one residence in northeast Mexico with weather information obtained from OpenWeather. The research team uses a WiFi energy meter and Raspberry Pi collection system to record active, reactive and apparent power, current, voltage and power factor. The article reports 605,260 one-minute observations with nineteen fields from 5 November 2022–5 January 2024. Mendeley provides a single CSV free under CC BY 4.0. Weather variables include temperature, pressure, humidity, wind and categorical conditions, alongside next-day temperature forecasts. Those forecast fields must not be interpreted as contemporaneous observations. Coverage is limited to one household, and the public repository description does not identify an exact city or establish representative occupancy. A reviewer-assessed use is checking weather-sensitive residential-load components or short-horizon demand scenarios. model-energyplus is a related building simulator, but building geometry and construction inputs would be needed separately. No measurement file or prediction model was run.
